links.note: The Upanishads introducing atman as divine and one with brahman, and the interconnectedness that follows from it - both the assertion and the reason are sentences of this concept. Already linked and correct.

A seeker striving to realise a universal divine essence pervading all existence is Upanishadic and Vedantic thought, which this concept sets out as brahman, atman and their oneness; early Vedic ritualism and Charvaka materialism are the distractors the chapter also names.
Shvetaketu learning about brahman from Uddalaka Aruni, from the Chhandogya Upanishad - this concept tells that story. Already linked and correct.

The Charvaka or Lokayata school, which held that this material world is the only thing that exists and that there can be no life after death, and which did not gain much popularity and disappeared with time - this concept says both, which is why the assertion is false and the reason true.

A monk as a man who gives up the usual life in the world for religious or spiritual pursuits and takes vows, with a nun as the female equivalent - both are glossed in this concept alongside bhikshus and bhikshunis.
The Toda tribals of the Nilgiris, for whom over thirty peaks of the range are residences of a god or goddess, so sacred that they avoid pointing at them - this concept's example.

Spiritual glossed as concerned with the spirit or soul, atman, with spirituality as the search for a deeper dimension beyond our current personality - this concept places that gloss before anything else in the chapter.
The false pair is ritam as a poetic meter; this concept defines ritam as truth and order in human life and in the cosmos, which is what makes the option wrong.
The Constitution using the terms tribes and tribal communities in English and janjati in Hindi - this concept states that explicitly.
The Rig Veda as the most ancient of the four Vedas - this concept names all four and singles it out. Already linked and correct.
Bhikshus as the monks of the Sangha the Buddha founded, with bhikshunis or nuns added later - this concept's account. Already linked and correct.
Revering a mountain as the abode of spirits reflects the belief this concept states - that mountains, rivers, trees and even stones are sacred because there is consciousness behind all of them.

The rigorous training behind the oral transmission and its result, hymns passed down with hardly any alterations - this concept is the one that weighs what that transmission is worth. Already linked and correct.
The false pair makes ritam mean material possessions; this concept defines ritam as truth and order in human life and in the cosmos, and also supplies janas, another of the options.
Vedic chanting recognised as intangible heritage, the term used because what is recognised is a practice and not a text - this concept's point. Already linked and correct.
Aham brahmasmi asserting the divine nature within the individual - this concept is where atman is defined as the divine essence residing in every being and ultimately one with brahman.
Veda meaning knowledge, from the Sanskrit vid - this concept's etymology.
The Rig Veda as the most ancient of the four - this concept says so while noting how widely its date is disputed. Already linked and correct.
The hymns composed by rishis, male seers, and rishikas, female ones - this concept gives both terms. Already linked and correct.
Brahman, or sometimes just tat, as the one divine essence in Vedanta - this concept gives both words.
Aham brahmasmi meaning I am brahman - this concept holds the atman and brahman identity that the mantra states.
Siddhartha Gautama born in Lumbini, today in Nepal - this concept's opening.
Buddha meaning the enlightened or awakened one - this concept's closing gloss after the enlightenment at Bodh Gaya.
Ahimsa generally translated as non-violence, originally non-hurting or non-injuring - this concept's gloss. Already linked and correct.
The Sangha as the community of bhikshus and later bhikshunis the Buddha founded - this concept's sentence.
Vardhamana born into a royal family near Vaishali - this concept's account of his birth. Already linked and correct.
Jina meaning conqueror, of ignorance and attachments rather than of territory or enemies - this concept's DON'T MISS OUT box.
Anekantavada meaning not just one aspect or perspective, the truth having many aspects - this concept's second principle. Already linked and correct.
Aparigraha advising non-possession and detachment from material possessions - this concept's third principle. Already linked and correct.
The significance of the 2008 UNESCO recognition of Vedic chanting as a masterpiece of oral and intangible heritage - this concept's box. Already linked and correct.
Explaining atman as the Self, the divine essence residing within every being and ultimately one with brahman - this concept's definition, word for word.
